To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ruminal acidosis induced in sheep by feeding wheat grains at 90 g/kg body weight caused alterations in the physicochemical properties of rumen liquor, serum, CSF and the urine.

the ruminal acidosis in sheep was associated with decreased rumen pH and increased rumen lactic acid concentrations, decreased pH and increased lactic acid concentrations and decreased levels of sodium, chloride, potassium and calcium and increased inorganic phosphorus levels in the blood.

lactic acidosis induced by wheat grain feeding in sheep is associated with alterations in the pH of rumen liquor, CSF, blood and urine and in the concentration of sodium, potassium, calcium, chloride, inorganic phosphates, glucose and total leucocytes in the CSF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathogenesis of acidotic conditions in sheep and the effect of acidotic conditions on the blood, CSF, urine and rumen liquor of sheep.
the changes in the physicochemical properties of blood, CSF, and urine in sheep suffering from lactic acidosis.
the pathogenesis of lactic acidosis and the changes that occur in the blood, CSF, and urine in sheep with lactic acidosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the biochemical changes in blood, CS F and urine in experimental acidosis are similar in sheep to those observed in human beings.
the changes in the blood, CSF, urine and Pandy's test in sheep with lactic acidosis are similar to those reported in the literature in other species of domestic animals.
the changes in blood and CSF parameters in the present study were similar to those reported in other species of experimental lactic acidotic animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lactic acidosis causes alterations in the blood and CSF pH and in the concentrations of various electrolytes in serum, CSF and in urine.

lactic acidosis is associated with changes in the levels of electrolytes, glucose, inorganic phosphates, leucocyte counts, Pandy's test and other parameters in the rumen, blood, cerebrosinal fluid and urine of sheep.
lactic acidosis causes a decrease in pH in ruminal liquor, blood, urine and CSF and an increase in total lactic acid levels in ruminal liquor and blood, urine and cerebrospinal fluids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biochemical alterations in blood, CS F and urine are similar to those in human beings.
the changes in the biochemical profile of blood, CSF, and urine in the sheep model of ruminal acidosis were comparable to the changes seen in the human model of lactic acidosis.
the lactic acidosis induced by wheat grain feeding in sheep is associated with alterations in the blood, CSF, and urine.
